anomalies.observed: SW6 is a two-circuit DIP switch. Its first switch connects the far ends of R34 and R35, which are otherwise on /CAN0_N and /CAN1_N; its second switch connects /CAN1_P and /CAN0_P. Thus, closing the switches couples the two CAN buses instead of independently terminating each bus across its own P/N pair.
anomalies.expected: Keep CAN0 and CAN1 electrically independent. If SW6 is intended to select termination, each switch should connect a 120-ohm resistor across the corresponding bus's P and N nets.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller

anomalies.impact: Closing the switches can couple the two nominally isolated CAN interfaces, causing bus interference or communication failures; the resistors also do not provide the expected independent P-to-N termination.

parsed.summary: Anomaly detected: SW6's wiring couples the two CAN buses when its switches are closed, rather than providing independent termination for CAN0 and CAN1. This conflicts with the specified separate, isolated CAN interfaces.
